native_result.query: How does the effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP compare between developing countries and countries in Sub-Saharan Africa?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it
native_result.HypoB: In these two World Bank aggregates (LMC proxying developing countries; SSF for Sub-Saharan Africa), there is no robust, sign-consistent effect of increasing the education-expenditure share of GNI on per-capita income in either group, and no reliable evidence that the effect differs between them: LMC long-run level associations are negative but trend-driven (DW~0.2-0.4), LMC year-over-year associations are small and positive but fragile (+2 to +3% GNI per +1pp, sign-flipping with controls/lags), and SSA can only be estimated over 2011-2015 (n=5), where a mechanically negative slope (-10% per +1pp) arises because the education share fell while GNI drifted up. The pooled interaction comparison (SSF -10% vs LMC -66% per +1pp, n=10) is a small-sample trend artifact and is treated as secondary. Caveats: GNI (constant 2015 US$) analyzed rather than GDP (2010 US$), education measured as % of GNI rather than % of total expenditure, LMC stands in for 'developing countries', and aggregate two-unit data support associational claims only.
native_result.WorkflowB: Wide CSV reshaped to a group-year panel (2 groups x 6 series x 41 years); completeness audited (SSF GNI only 2011-2015, n=5; LMC complete); asymmetric-window estimation per researcher instruction: (1) LMC full-sample OLS with Newey-West HAC SEs, (2) LMC first-differenced regressions (bivariate, enrollment controls, all controls, lagged-educ split, 5-yr MA FD) as primary evidence, (3) SSF bivariate slope on its 2011-2015 GNI window, (4) pooled interaction model on the 2011-2015 overlap (n=10) as secondary; Durbin-Watson diagnostics on every model; effect sizes reported as % change in GNI pc per +1pp education-expenditure share; script analysis_worldbank_education_gdp.py, log outputs/analysis_results.txt.
